Hexagon shot chart: where they shoot from, and how well

Source: R/shots.R
plot_shot_hex.Rd

Kirk Goldsberry-style chart. Hexagon size is how often the player shoots from that spot, hexagon colour is FG% compared with the league from the same spot (shrunk, so tiny samples stay near white). Faceting by facet gives small multiples on a common scale.

Usage

plot_shot_hex(
  shots,
  baseline = shots,
  facet = NULL,
  league = NULL,
  binwidth = 0.75,
  min_attempts = 3,
  fill = c("fg", "pps"),
  limit = NULL,
  max_size = 1,
  title = NULL,
  subtitle = NULL,
  caption = NULL
)

Arguments

shots

Shot data (see Details in plot_shot_hex()).

baseline

Shots used for the league reference; defaults to shots. Pass the whole league so a single player is compared with everyone.

facet

Column to facet by (also used for binning).

league

Court to draw; defaults to the league in the data.

binwidth

Distance between hexagon centres, in metres.

min_attempts

Hide hexagons with fewer attempts (they carry no information about efficiency and clutter the court).

fill

"fg" (FG% vs league) or "pps" (points per shot vs league).

limit

Colour scale limit (+-).

max_size

Largest hexagon as a fraction of the full hexagon.

title, subtitle, caption

Labels. A default subtitle explains the encoding.

Details

Shot data needs x, y in metres from the hoop centre (y towards half court), made, and optionally value and league. See as_ggbasket_shots() to take shots out of a play-by-play.

Examples

curry <- subset(shots_2024, player == "Stephen Curry")
plot_shot_hex(curry, baseline = subset(shots_2024, league == "NBA"),
              title = "Stephen Curry, 2024/25")
